reason: A is the better proposal because it gives a directional, falsifiable link between oxide-phase/scale-integrity changes and corrosion across the two temperature regimes, although its assumed protective room-temperature magnetite scale requires verification and better controls to isolate temperature from salt-state effects. B largely repeats the cited Q235 passivation study and makes the high-temperature prediction noncommittal (“either” outcome), while its N/F-rich film is unlikely to remain a meaningful mediator at 700–900 °C.
